question: When should an integration use SEP-6, SEP-24, or SEP-31 for fiat on/off-ramp and cross-border flows?

golden.answer: Use SEP-24 when the anchor hosts the interactive deposit and withdrawal UI. Use SEP-6 for a programmatic API with no hosted UI; only SEP-6's old interactive flow is deprecated in favor of SEP-24. Use SEP-31 for anchor-to-anchor cross-border payments, where a sending anchor pays a receiving anchor with no end-user UI. SEP-38 adds quotes. SEP-6, SEP-24 and SEP-31 are all Active as of 2026-11-14; SEP-38 is Draft.
keyFacts: SEP-24 is the anchor-hosted interactive deposit and withdrawal standard.
SEP-6 is the programmatic API; only its interactive flow is deprecated.
SEP-31 is a sending anchor paying a receiving anchor, with no end-user hosted UI.
SEP-6, SEP-24 and SEP-31 are Active standards (as of a stated date).
avoid: Do NOT claim SEP-31 replaces both SEP-6 and SEP-24.
Do NOT claim SEP-24 requires the wallet to host the anchor's KYC user interface.
golden.notes: Quoting official docs on SEP-6 programmatic use without the interactive deprecation is not a wrong claim while sd-009 stands; the grade caps at partial for that claim.

corroboration.claim: SEP-24 is the anchor-hosted interactive deposit/withdrawal flow; SEP-6 is the programmatic deposit/withdrawal API.
SEP-6 remains Active; its legacy interactive flow, not the whole SEP, is deprecated in favor of SEP-24.
SEP-31 has a Sending Anchor call a Receiving Anchor under an established bilateral/commercial relationship.
SEP-6, SEP-24, and SEP-31 are Active as of 2026-11-02; SEP-38 (Draft) applies when quotes/rates are part of the corridor.
